kind: new edit of one shared licensed source film
promptSource: Exact creative request, unchanged; full request includes shared delivery and review instructions
creativePrompt: Use only the supplied Tears of Steel source video to make a 12-second widescreen action edit called Velocity. Inspect the source first and choose four genuinely energetic shots with clear camera or subject motion; avoid dialogue-only holds and credits. Build a readable arc: 0–2s an intriguing moving detail, 2–5s three escalating action cuts, 5–8s one hero movement that eases from 100% to 45% speed for its peak then accelerates to 220%, 8–11s a decisive payoff, 11–12s a clean visual finish. Cut on matching movement directions and use two 6-frame whip transitions only where source motion supports them. Add a single 6% punch-in on the strongest impact. Preserve sharp faces and edges; use frame sampling if interpolation bends objects. Keep original environmental sound where useful, add a restrained original percussive pulse and two synchronized impacts, and duck the pulse under any retained intelligible speech. No stock footage, no new generated scenes, no full-screen captions, and no random flash/glitch effects. Deliver one polished 1920x1080 H264 MP4 with intentional crops, no stretched image, plus source timecodes and an edit decision list. The edit must still clearly communicate acceleration and payoff when muted.

sourceFootage.title: Tears of Steel
sourceFootage.modifications: Acceleration, a slow-motion peak, and cuts that follow the action.

deliveryMethod: Durable Luna high targeted repair and host delivery
review: Continuous smoothstep speed1→0.45→2.2 and integrated source-time map independently evaluated; source and speed joins are continuous, with smooth2.2→1 payoff return.
Final implementation uses six-frame whips88–93 and116–121, one-based overlay(n-1)/5 and zero-based maskN/5; translation ends at0 and mask becomes opaque.
Independently decoded candidate frames86–95 and114–123 show no retained outgoing strip, black gap, or prior10percent tail-registration snap.
Independently decoded ramp frames149–250 show advancing source motion and no interpolation deformation; code-derived timing establishes continuous acceleration, beyond what stills alone can show.
Both settled punch branches scale2034x1144 then center-crop1920x1080. Encoded frames327–333 show continuing source motion without an additional scale reset.
Final candidate hash matches the author repair_checks ledger.

kind: new edit of one shared licensed source film
promptSource: Exact creative request, unchanged; full request includes shared delivery and review instructions
creativePrompt: Turn the same supplied Tears of Steel source into a 12-second widescreen moving film poster. Choose one continuous shot with at least 6 seconds of usable motion with a clear expressive character or striking mechanical silhouette. Start full-screen in motion for 2.5s; stop precisely on the strongest pose with a clean 8-frame camera ease, then animate the frozen image into a large offset rectangular crop over a warm ivory background. Reveal three small close-up tiles from that exact same frame—an eye or face detail, a mechanical detail, and a texture—with precise staggered slides. Use bold condensed black typography reading 'A MOMENT / IN MOTION', one small burnt-orange index '01', and thin alignment rules. Keep the frozen hero recognizably photographic and let scale/position supply depth; do not attempt a rough automatic cutout. Hold the completed editorial poster from 6.5–9s, then resolve the tiles into the full original frame and resume its source motion from the exact held frame for the final 3s. Use restrained dry camera clicks and the source ambience. No footage beyond the one source. Deliver 1920x1080 H264 MP4, crisp type, generous margins, no unreadable microtext, source timecodes, and the edit decision list.

sourceFootage.title: Tears of Steel
sourceFootage.modifications: A moving shot becomes an editorial poster, then returns to motion.

deliveryMethod: Author container rendering and verified host upload
review: Critical encoded frames 74/75/76/83 show continuous shot entering frozen poster; short layered transition is intentional and resolves cleanly.
Poster has readable condensed two-line title, warm ivory board, orange 01, thin rules, and three distinct same-pose detail crops. No visible clipping or stretched subject.
Encoded frames 195,216,269 show stable completed poster through the required 6.5–9 second hold.
Frames 270/271 begin the poster resolve; 285,315,359 show returned full-frame shot and advancing motion without a visible source-shot jump.
Metadata confirms 12 seconds, 360 decoded frames, 1920x1080 H264 30fps and stereo 48kHz AAC. Cloud review independently confirms byte range and faststart.

kind: new edit of one shared licensed source film
promptSource: Exact creative request, unchanged; full request includes shared delivery and review instructions
creativePrompt: Create a 12-second 1920x1080 widescreen editorial split-screen film using only the same supplied Tears of Steel source. Pick one short sequence with a clear subject and useful wide, medium, and close-up views. Open as one uninterrupted full-width shot for 1.5s. Slide two thin cream dividers into place over 0.5s to reveal a deliberate 25% / 50% / 25% triptych: left is an environment or gesture detail, center is the hero action, right is a face or mechanical detail. Use different source moments or crops, never three identical copies; align the most important actions to meet at 5s. At 6s smoothly transfer the center panel's dominance to the right by resizing the panels over 12 frames, maintaining every subject's framing. At 9s make a clean synchronized match cut across all three panels. From 10.5–12s expand the strongest panel to full screen and finish on a satisfying moving frame. White balance all panels coherently and use warm off-white 5px gutters, no rounded app-card styling. Retain a continuous source ambience with gentle edit accents. No captions except small optional '01', '02', '03' outside faces. Deliver the MP4 and exact crop/timecode decisions. Every panel must visibly contribute a different view.

sourceFootage.modifications: Three views share the frame and exchange emphasis.

Frames149/150 show distinct source moments and crops with coherent cool white balance, fine warm cream dividers, and no obvious stretched subject.
Frames179/180/186/192 show the center-to-right geometry transfer settling into 25/25/50 at6.4 seconds; mechanical/rifle detail remains visible during the transfer.

Before-cut frame269 shows three active face views. Later314/315 show synchronized alternate content in all three panels; exact frame270 cut is not independently established because frame270 appears very similar to269 in the critical sheet.
Frames315/359 show the dominant right panel expanding into full width; final facial expression has changed, providing visible evidence of continuing source motion.

kind: new edit of one shared licensed source film
promptSource: Exact creative request, unchanged; full request includes shared delivery and review instructions
creativePrompt: Create a 10-second cinematic color transformation from the same supplied Tears of Steel source. Select one continuous shot with a face, strong practical lights or glowing machinery, and meaningful shadow detail. For the first 1.25s show the untouched source. Then let a thin vertical comparison edge travel from left to right over 1.25s, revealing a carefully balanced nocturnal grade: deep cool shadows, warm controlled highlights, natural skin, gentle highlight rolloff, and readable blacks. During 2.5–7.5s give the graded image a very restrained 4% camera push while keeping the shot continuous and preserving its actual action. In the final 2.5s show a concise moving 50/50 original-versus-grade comparison with small crisp 'SOURCE' and 'AFTER DARK' labels in the lower safe area. The change must be obvious but tasteful—no crushed eyes, orange faces, excessive saturation, faux scratches, or synthetic grain. Do not call an already graded source LOG and do not add fake camera metadata. Preserve source ambience and use no new music. Deliver one 1920x1080 H264 MP4 plus source timecode and a concise list of the actual grading adjustments.

sourceFootage.modifications: A moving comparison reveals cool shadows and controlled warm highlights.
